title: SDK docs: add streaming troubleshooting (timeouts, reconnect, idempotency) and align language across Python/TS/Go
creator: Elliot Price
project: Customer Success & Support: escalation playbook refresh + known-issues sprint (2026-02)
description: Add a consistent, copy/paste-ready troubleshooting section for streaming responses across SDK docs (Python/TypeScript/Go). Cover: (1) timeouts and client-side settings, (2) safe reconnect + retry/backoff patterns, (3) idempotency guidance and request ID collection for Support. Ensure language matches the Known Issues workaround article and Support macros so customers see one coherent set of steps.
background: Support escalations (e.g., SUP-1842, SUP-1854) show repeated confusion around "stream reset" vs "truncated output" and what is safe to retry. Today, each SDK doc mentions streaming briefly but lacks clear operational guidance (timeouts, keepalive/proxy behavior, idempotency, what to send Support). This is causing longer time-to-triage and repeat tickets. This ticket is part of the Known Issues sprint to publish workarounds and link them consistently from Support workflows.
scope: 1) Add a "Troubleshooting streaming" section to the SDK docs surface (Python/TS/Go). 2) Standardize terminology: "disconnect/reset" vs "truncated stream"; emphasize request IDs; include a minimal checklist for Support. 3) Cross-link to the Known Issues article on streaming timeouts/reconnect. 4) Add clear "When to escalate" callouts consistent with Support severity triggers (without exposing internal thresholds).
out_of_scope: Changing runtime/gateway behavior (handled in ENG-4822 / PRs in redwood). Building new SDK-level retry middleware beyond docs/examples. Publishing customer-specific details or incident timelines.
acceptance_criteria: A) Each SDK guide contains a Streaming Troubleshooting section with the same structure and consistent phrasing. B) Includes explicit guidance on timeout configuration, reconnect/retry patterns, and idempotency considerations. C) Includes a short "Send this to Support" checklist (region, model, SDK version, approximate timestamp, request IDs). D) Cross-links to the Known Issues KB article and uses the same recommended mitigations (retry/backoff; consider keepalive/proxy settings; avoid unsafe retries). E) Reviewed by Support + SRE for correctness and customer-safe language.
proposed_structure: Section template (used in Python/TS/Go): 1) Symptoms (disconnect/reset, truncated stream, long stalls). 2) Quick checks (SDK version, proxy/load balancer timeouts, client read timeout). 3) Recommended retry pattern (exponential backoff + jitter; max attempts; only retry safe operations; consider idempotency keys where supported). 4) Timeouts + keepalive guidance (client read timeout, TCP keepalive; note HTTP/2/proxy behavior). 5) When to escalate (persistent failures across attempts, multi-region impact, high error rates; include request IDs). 6) Links (Known Issues article + status page guidance).
content_notes: Key language decisions to keep consistent across SDKs: - Use "streaming disconnect/reset" for mid-generation connection drops; use "truncated output" for premature end-of-stream. - Recommend retry/backoff with jitter; do NOT recommend tight loops or unbounded retries. - Idempotency: remind customers that retrying a generation call can produce different outputs; if their application requires exactly-once semantics, they must design for it (store partials, use idempotency keys where available, avoid repeating side effects). - Always request IDs: include how to capture from response headers / SDK debug logs; point to Support intake checklist for what to send.
implementation_plan: Docs work lives in redwood-docs. Add a shared partial/snippet (or duplicated but identical text blocks) to keep Python/TS/Go aligned. Include short code examples per language (set timeout; stream loop; retry wrapper). Add cross-links to Known Issues hub + streaming workaround article. Ensure the new section is discoverable via nav and search (add keywords: streaming timeout, reconnect, disconnect, reset, truncated).
testing_and_validation: 1) Docs build passes. 2) Copy edits for consistency across languages. 3) Support review for "what to ask for" and customer-safe mitigation steps. 4) SRE spot-check that recommendations don’t conflict with incident response guidance (no bypassing on-call process; no suggesting internal dashboards).
rollout_plan: Publish with the Known Issues hub rollout. After merge, Support to add link into macros/snippets for streaming issues and Jira triage automation prompt (INT-333). Track deflection: number of streaming tickets lacking request IDs; time-to-first-action; repeat tickets per account.
